generated_by: session-authored from 10-K MD&A segment tables, verified by agreement across overlapping filings
summary: Health insurer, pharmacy benefit manager and retail pharmacy in one filer. The three measures below are the ones CVS manages the business on and XBRL does not carry: the medical benefit ratio for the Health Care Benefits segment, and pharmacy volume for Pharmacy & Consumer Wellness.

metrics.label: Medical Benefit Ratio (reported)
metrics.why: The ratio CVS itself publishes for the Health Care Benefits segment, and the one its results are discussed on. Distinct from the Loss Ratio row above, which is a consolidated GAAP construction.
metrics.evidence: Health Care Benefits segment table, MD&A: 91.2% / 92.5% / 86.2% for FY2025 / FY2024 / FY2023.

metrics.label: Pharmacy Claims Processed (reported)
metrics.why: Pharmacy & Consumer Wellness volume, the denominator behind that segment's economics.
metrics.evidence: Pharmacy & Consumer Wellness table, MD&A: 1,900.7m / 1,917.6m / 2,344.3m for FY2025 / FY2024 / FY2023.

metrics.label: Prescriptions Filled (reported)
metrics.why: The same volume on a 90-day-adjusted basis, which is how CVS reports script growth.
metrics.evidence: Pharmacy & Consumer Wellness table, MD&A: 1,808.8m / 1,715.5m / 1,649.1m for FY2025 / FY2024 / FY2023.

annotations.loss_ratio: A consolidated GAAP construction, not the ratio CVS reports: PolicyholderBenefitsAndClaimsIncurredNet over PremiumsEarnedNet, both across the whole company. For Q2 FY2026 it comes to 89.7% where CVS reported a medical benefit ratio of 87.4%. Neither is wrong; they answer different questions. The MBR row below carries the company's own figure, which is scoped to the Health Care Benefits segment and uses CVS's definition of health care costs.

caveats: None of these three is XBRL-tagged, so all come from MD&A tables. There is no filed value to reconcile against, so each year is verified instead by agreement across filings: every 10-K prints three years, consecutive filings overlap on two, and a year is accepted only where a filing reporting it agrees with a year already established. The oldest filing in the window seeds the series and is taken on its own.

The MBR row cannot be anchored on its own name. "Medical benefit ratio" appears five times in the FY2025 10-K — forward-looking statements, risk factors, and twice in the commentary defining it — and never immediately before the figures, because the row label wraps. The anchor is the tail of its parenthetical, "premium revenues)", followed by three percentages.

Annual only. The 10-Q layout has not been checked, so quarter cells stay blank rather than being filled from a pattern whose column order is unconfirmed — the mistake that put a quarterly figure in an annual column elsewhere in this app.
